Questions.QuestionText: Which of the following is NOT a type of Tetra?
Questions.AnswerFact: The Zebra Tetra is not a real fish, while the other three are recognised types of tetras commonly found in the aquarium trade.

Questions.QuestionText: What type of fish is pictured here?
Questions.AnswerFact: The Atlantic Blue Marlin can grow up to 14 feet long, and weigh nearly 2,000 pounds. Both the Sailfish and Blue Marlin belong to the Istiophoriformes order, which also includes the closely related Swordfish.

Questions.QuestionText: Which of the following fish is typically the largest species in the world?
Questions.AnswerFact: The Whale Shark is a slow-moving, filter-feeding carpet shark, and is the largest species of fish in the world. They can reach lengths up to 18m (60ft) in length and weigh between 11 and 21 tons. Some extinct fish, such as the Leedsicthys (pictured), were even larger.

Questions.QuestionText: Which fish species was caught in the largest quantity worldwide by weight in 2022?
Questions.AnswerFact: In 2022, approximately 4.9 million tons worth of Peruvian Anchovies were caught, making them the most caught fish species worldwide by weight. The 2nd most caught by weight in 2022 was the Alaska Pollock, at 3.4 million tons.
Sources: Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations

Questions.QuestionText: Atlantic, Pacific and Greenland are all types of which fish species?
Questions.AnswerFact: Atlantic Cod, Pacific Cod and Greenland Cod are all species within the cod family (Gadidae). Pollock is also part of the Cod family, but is usually referred to by its own name rather than 'cod'.

Questions.QuestionText: As of 2025, what is the conservation status of the Tiger Shark?
Questions.AnswerFact: The International Union for Conservation of Nature (IUCN) lists the Tiger Shark as Near Threatened due to overfishing, shark finning, and population declines in parts of its range.

Questions.QuestionText: Which of the following fish is venomous?
Questions.AnswerFact: Lionfish are venomous marine fish native to the Indo-Pacific. They possess potent, protein-based venom in their needle-like spines used for defence against predators. Fugu Pufferfish aren't venomous, but are poisonous if improperly prepared and eaten.

Questions.QuestionText: What is the deepest depth a living fish has been found?
Questions.AnswerFact: The deepest depth a living fish has been found was at 8,336m (27,349ft). The fish in question was a Mariana Snailfish (pictured), and was filmed by scientists in the Izu-Ogasawara Trench, south of Japan.
